newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-Nomura president indicted over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Nomura president indicted over scandal.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors said on Thursday they had indicted a former president of Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Hideo Sakamaki, on charges of making illegal payoffs to a racketeer.

Sakamaki was arrested late last month on suspicion of conspiring with three former Nomura executives to make illegal payoffs to "sokaiya" racketeer Ryuichi Koike in 1995, in violation of the securities law. Sokaiya extort money by threatening to disrupt shareholders meetings.

The indictment alleges that Sakamaki paid 49.73 million yen ($440,000) to Koike between January 31 and June 15, 1995. Sakamaki resigned from the top post at Nomura, Japan's biggest brokerage, in March over the scandal, which has also embroiled top Japanese bank Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB).

Nomura itself has already been indicted on suspicion of violating the securities law by compensating a firm owned by Koike's brother for trading losses. Two former Nomura directors have been indicted on charges of making payoffs to Koike through his brother's firm in return for not disrupting Nomura shareholders meetings. The two brothers have also been arrested.

The scandal, which has now led to the arrests of five Nomura officials, including Sakamaki, and 10 DKB officials, is unfolding just as Japan kicks off its "Big Bang" reforms of its long-protected financial sector.

Sakamaki's indictment could pave the way for the Japanese financial authorities to make a swift decision on punishment of the brokerage, which is likely to be ordered to suspend some of its business for up to six months. ($1=113 yen)
